question.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}?$
question.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{6}{7} & \frac{2}{7} & \frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{6}{7} \\ 0 & \frac{2}{7} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot 0=0.$
